verdict.line: You lose if Camille forces short all-ins off Hookshot (E) before your level-9 item spike; you win if you survive to Sunfire Aegis plus Thornmail and convert with Call of the Forge God (R) in skirmishes.

brief.thesis: Camille's kit is built around short, decisive trades — Precision Protocol (Q) empowered autos and Hookshot (E) engage/disengage — while Ornn has no tool to punish a hit-and-run before level 6. The 49.5% win rate over 1385 games against a measured lane and solo-kill deficit means this is a lane you survive, not win, until your core items and Call of the Forge God (R) come online.

theirWindow.what: She can follow with a delayed Precision Protocol recast for the increased bonus damage, then Tactical Sweep's outer-half slow and heal to extend the trade. Do not stand and fight this chain — disengage or use Bellows Breath to advance and close the gap on your terms instead.

yourWindow.what: Adaptive Defenses only shields after a landed basic attack and only lasts briefly, so once it drops, step in with Volcanic Rupture (Q) for the slow and follow with Searing Charge (E) toward terrain for the knockup.

powerCurve.note: Her Q cooldown is shorter, wins short trades
Hookshot engage lands before your items matter
Your R threatens her all-in, 140s cooldown limits it
Sunfire Aegis and Thornmail outscale her sustain
R recast knockup wins teamfights, not duels

start.why: Measured as the stronger start here (51.2% over 941 games, 59.2% pick) — the passive sustain directly counters the short trades Camille is built to win.

boots.why: Her entire trade pattern runs through basic attacks — the Precision Protocol empowered auto and the Adaptive Defenses shield it triggers. Steelcaps blunts that at 51.1% over 1230 games, the clear preferred pick (82.3%).

core.why: First item in the best-performing path (51.3% over 39 games); gives you the health and sustained damage to survive to your real power spike.
Directly answers the healing she gets off Tactical Sweep's outer-half hit — grievous wounds shuts down her only sustain tool.
Closes out the measured core path; stacking resistances turns you from a lane liability into a teamfight wall by level 13-ish.

situational.when: she builds toward on-hit magic damage or you're facing more magic threats on her team
you're already ahead and want the extra sustain in prolonged skirmishes over raw armor
her early Tactical Sweep heal is winning trades before you can afford full Thornmail

runes.keystoneWhy: This page measures highest here (52.9% over sample, 11.8% pick) — Font of Life and Second Wind stack extra sustain against a lane that's built to punish you in short trades.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the higher measured win rate here (51% over the sample) — Ignite cuts through her Tactical Sweep heal and the Adaptive Defenses shield during her all-in window. Flash+Teleport is the more popular pick (71.5%) if you'd rather play for the scaling lane instead of contesting early kill pressure.

playing.title: Trade short, not long
playing.detail: Her Precision Protocol (Q, 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown) rewards extended fights with a delayed, bigger-damage recast. Hit and reset before that window opens instead of standing in a trade.

playing.title: Play off walls, not on them
playing.detail: Hookshot (E, 800 range, 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown) requires her to pull to terrain to leap and knock up. Staying off walls in lane removes her main engage and the solo-kill risk the data shows.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed Tactical Sweep
playing.detail: Her W fires after a delay and only slows/heals if the outer half connects. If she whiffs it, her cooldown (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) is dead time — step in with Volcanic Rupture (Q) or Searing Charge (E).

playing.title: Don't trade into her shield
playing.detail: Adaptive Defenses shields her off a landed basic attack. Per OP.GG's read, retreat when that shield is visibly up and re-engage once it drops — your damage is wasted against it.

playing.title: Don't feed Q into her Ultimatum
playing.detail: Her R (Hextech Ultimatum) can absorb an incoming ability when she casts it on you. Hold Volcanic Rupture until after the anchor resolves rather than throwing it the instant she dashes in.

playing.title: Use W to close the gap, then set up R
playing.detail: Bellows Breath lets you advance through her — land the final gout to apply Brittle before you commit Searing Charge or wait for Call of the Forge God, since you don't have the mobility to catch her otherwise.

playing.title: Don't expect R as an early bailout
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God starts at a 140s cooldown and only reaches 100s at rank 3 — you're on your own in early all-ins, which is exactly why the lane-phase numbers favor her.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own read on why those numbers come out this way.

stats.opponentTip: Ignore Camille’s (E) with your [W] when engaging combat. Retreat when she has her (P) shield, and close in once it is deactivated. Camille’s (R) can be used to absorb an ability.
